newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes up on weather and exports, KCBT.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes up on weather and exports, KCBT.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on renewed concerns about weather problems in portions of the U.S. crop, export hopes and on a strong rally in KCBT wheat futures, traders said.
The Kansas City market rallied on a decline in the amount of deliverable-grade wheat in Kansas City elevators, KCBT traders said.
The export chat-mill was fueled by news from several fronts including Algeria and Pakistan.
"Algeria held a snap tender and Pakistan only has nine days of wheat stocks," a trader said.
European grain traders Tuesday said Algeria launched a snap tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. and/or Canadian wheat.
Pakistan Tuesday called for its citizens to buy less food and not to hoard after three days of food riots and protests in two provinces sparked by a scarcity of wheat.
Wheat futures closed 1-1/2 to four cents per bushel higher, with May up 1-1/2 at $3.82.
Wheat futures also found support on persistent talk about potential delays in seeding the U.S. spring wheat crop and on cold weather in portions of the U.S. winter wheat growing region.
"It's turnaround Tuesday but not in wheat where we have weather worries in the Southwest and Northern plains," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook called for below-normal temperatures and above-normal precipitation in most of the U.S. Northern Midwest spring wheat growing region.
In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did two million bushels of July/May at two cents, traders said.

In the wheat futures pit, Refco Inc sold five million bushels of July and bought three million July, traders said. E.D. and F. Man International sold two million bushels of July and Tenco Inc sold one million bushels of July, traders said. Farmers Commodities Corp bought 1.8 million bushels of July and Prudential Securities bought 2.5 million bushels of May, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 23,000, above the 21,375 traded Monday.

In wheat options, Smith Barney sold 200 July $3.60 puts at nine cents, Prudential Securities bought 200 May $4.00 calls at 2-1/2 cents and Refco Inc bought 200 May $4.00 calls at 3-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, up from the 9,665 traded Monday.
